abstraction_design.rationale: The low-level helpers were genuinely designed around the app's real variation (options callbacks, derived species maps) and stretch well. But there is no detail-page abstraction above them, so a Moves-shaped Items section is copy-paste of renderMove, and the moves panel shows early flag/state creep.

findings.issue: main.js is a monolith: router, five page renderers, the moves subsystem, sorting, and event wiring in one 876-line file
findings.suggestion: Split into router.js plus one module per page (or per feature: home.js, pokemon.js, moves.js, types.js); removal and extension scenarios then become file deletions/additions

findings.issue: The Moves feature (~180 lines: prepareMoves, loadRowsForGame, movesPanelHtml, attachMovesHandlers) is embedded in the router file rather than its own module
findings.suggestion: Move to src/moves.js exporting renderMovesSection/attachHandlers; renderPokemon would compose it like the stats/evolution helpers

findings.issue: renderPokemon hand-builds the API path '/api/v2/pokemon/${species.id}/' as a fallback, duplicating api.js's URL-shape knowledge (resolveApiUrl's /api/v2/ prefix rule)
findings.suggestion: Add a pokemonUrl(id) (or speciesDefaultPokemonRef(species)) helper in api.js so URL construction stays in one module

findings.issue: The API base URL default ('http://localhost:9000') is duplicated in server.mjs and the client fallback at app/src/api.js:5
findings.suggestion: Have the server always inject the value (it already writes window.__API_BASE_URL__) and let the client treat a missing global as an error, or read both from one shared module

findings.issue: The 'replace panel HTML then re-attach handlers' pattern is duplicated verbatim in the game-change and sort-click handlers (also 454-460)
findings.suggestion: Extract a single refreshMovesPanel(state, token) helper both handlers call

findings.issue: '<count> Pokémon' + card-list section assembly is repeated at four call sites
findings.suggestion: Add a pokemonListPanel(title, cardSpecies, optionsForSpecies) helper in ui.js alongside panelHtml

findings.issue: Global mutable renderToken with manual token checks sprinkled through every async function is easy to forget in new code and silently reintroduces race bugs
findings.suggestion: Wrap navigation in a small controller that aborts in-flight work (AbortController passed to api()) or at minimum centralize the check in one guard function

findings.issue: detailsPanelHtml is a generic wrapper that only Move uses, and it lives in main.js instead of next to panelHtml in ui.js
findings.suggestion: Move it to ui.js (or fold it into panelHtml) so a new Items/Ability detail page naturally reuses it

summary: The data/rendering seam is well chosen: sprites, cards, panels and caching each live in one module, so the sprite bug fix and most card changes are single-point edits. Where it falls down is structure above that seam — main.js bundles the router, every page template and the entire moves feature into one 876-line file, making removal a scattershot edit and Moves-shaped additions (Items) a copy-paste job. Server and client are cleanly separated, with only the API base-URL default duplicated between them.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Three edits in one large file (delete renderAbility at 690, route branch at 807-809, abilities panel/links at 639-643) plus the .hidden-ability CSS rule at styles.css:259. No nav link exists to remove, and extractId stays used elsewhere, so no real dead code — but nothing is file-scoped, so removal is careful line surgery rather than deleting a module.

scenarios.change: Fix cards showing the wrong sprite when the default Pokémon's name differs (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Every card goes through pokemonCardHtml (ui.js:12-29) and every sprite URL through spriteUrl (api.js:83-85), so one fix covers all four lists (home, move 'Learned by', ability, type). If the correct sprite required the default Pokémon's own data rather than the id-pattern URL, the change stays in spriteUrl/pokemonCardHtml as long as the data layer supplies the species→default-pokemon mapping (data.js is the natural home).

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: pokemonCardListHtml (ui.js:33) is the single rendering seam for all four lists, so an optional comparator there covers everything at once. The mild friction is that ordering currently lives upstream — loadSpecies sorts by id (data.js:16-23) and speciesRefsByIds preserves id order — so a careless implementer could instead touch four call sites in main.js; the seam exists but isn't the obvious first place you'd look.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: api.js helpers (api, englishName, displayValue, humanize), panelHtml and detailsPanelHtml are reusable as-is, and data.js maps generalize if Items lists species. But renderMove (main.js:655-688) is a bespoke template, so the page body is a ~35-line copy-paste plus a new branch in renderRoute's if/else chain (main.js:786-811); a detail-page abstraction would make this a trivial addition.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: All fetching and the responseCache Map live in api.js (api.js:8, 34-57), so caching rules are a one-file change. The base URL needs two edits because the default 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in server.mjs:8 and the client fallback at api.js:5, though the runtime injection (server.mjs:22 → api.js:4) already handles the sane path; spriteUrl reuses the same constant, so media URLs follow automatically.
